item.title: China welcomes Japanese enterprises to develop business, share market opportunities in China: vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 -- China always welcomes Japanese enterprises to develop business and share market opportunities in the country, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng said on Tuesday. He, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when meeting with a delegation from Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade (JAPIT) in Beijing. Noting that China and Japan are close neighbors and important economic and trade partners to each other, He urged the JAPIT to keep to the right course on historical issues, continue to carry forward the tradition of friendship with China, and play a greater role in advancing China-Japan economic and trade cooperation. Takeshi Iwaya, president of JAPIT, said that Japan's business community is ready to further expand exchanges with China, and contribute to the continuous growth of bilateral economic and trade ties and deeper mutually beneficial cooperation.

item.title: China to accelerate green transformation during 2026-2030: vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 -- China will accelerate the all-round green transformation of its economic and social development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said on Tuesday. Ding, who is also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the chairperson of the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development (CCICED), made the remarks while addressing the 2026 annual general meeting of the CCICED in Beijing. Noting that China's tremendous achievements in ecological conservation have won international recognition, Ding said that during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, China will set bolder green and low-carbon development goals, adopt more robust measures, and establish a more rigorous institutional system. He called for joint efforts to take practical actions to promote green and low-carbon development and contribute to global climate governance and biodiversity conservation. He emphasized the importance of fostering green productivity through scientific and technological innovation, and improving global environmental and climate governance through openness and cooperation. China will as always strongly support the development of the CCICED, hoping all members and experts will continue to contribute their wisdom and strength to building a beautiful China and to global sustainable development, Ding said.

item.title: Xi urges Sichuan University to leverage strengths in serving national strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged Sichuan University to leverage its interdisciplinary strengths and play a pioneering and exemplary role in serving national strategies, as he extended congratulations on the 130th founding anniversary of the university. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to the university's teachers and students. In the letter, Xi congratulated the university's faculty members, students and alumni on the anniversary. He noted that serving the country with dedication, taking root in western China, and fostering talent through education are fine traditions of Sichuan University. Xi expressed the hope that the university will carry forward its revolutionary legacy, leverage its strengths of interdisciplinary integration across humanities, sciences, engineering and medicine, and contribute to building China into a leading country in education, science and technology, and talent development. The history of Sichuan University dates back to the Sichuan Chinese and Western School founded in 1896, the earliest institution of higher learning in southwest China.

item.title: Chinese premier urges solid workplace safety measures to prevent major accidents
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday called for solid and meticulous efforts in workplace safety to resolutely prevent and curb major accidents, and safeguard people's lives and property. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks at a national video conference on workplace safety. He noted that recent major and catastrophic accidents in some regions have caused serious losses to people's lives and property, highlighting the need for increased vigilance. Li called for intensifying fire prevention, strengthening safety management of mixed production and operation sites, strictly regulating outsourcing, and cracking down on illegal subcontracting and re-subcontracting. Emphasizing workplace safety in key industries and fields, Li urged efforts to strengthen whole-chain safety supervision of fireworks and firecrackers, carry out special rectification of coastal and river vessel enterprises, and enhance tourism and traffic safety management around the National Day holiday. He also underscored accident prevention in sectors including hazardous chemicals, industry and trade, and construction. The premier urged enterprises to comprehensively enhance workplace safety by accelerating the phase-out of outdated equipment and technological upgrading, and improving safety management systems. Stressing the importance of raising public awareness of workplace safety laws and knowledge, and fostering a safety culture, Li also urged efforts in disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, including monitoring and early warning, hazard inspection, duty shifts, and improving emergency plans so as to minimize disaster losses.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting on macro policies, investment
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday chaired a State Council executive meeting to discuss work related to strengthening and improving the effectiveness of macro policies and promoting effective investment. In response to emerging challenges in the economy's operation, efforts should be made to intensify counter-cyclical adjustment of macro policies and promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, the meeting noted, stressing that China will strive to achieve its annual economic and social development goals. The country has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for better results in practice. In the first half of 2026, the country's gross domestic product grew 4.7 percent. The meeting said that the issuance and utilization of various types of bonds will be accelerated, and major projects as specified in China's 15th Five-Year Plan and the "six networks" initiative, which covers water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, next-generation communication networks, urban underground pipeline networks and logistics networks, will be expedited in terms of project commencement. The meeting has urged efforts to advance the renovation and upgrading of aging and dilapidated reservoirs and grain depots, and implement policies designed to expand investment and boost consumption. According to the meeting, efforts will be made to optimize fiscal expenditure, adjust monetary policy tools in a timely manner, and increase relending support for scientific and technological innovation and technological transformation, agriculture and small businesses. Meanwhile, the government will examine and roll out policies and measures aimed at stabilizing the real estate market and promote employment and income growth, according to the meeting. Monday's meeting also heard a report on work related to the control of new pollutants, and deliberated and approved a draft regulation concerning the registration and management of public institutions.

item.title: Xi to pay tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders will present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning to mark the country's Martyrs' Day. The leaders will be joined by representatives from all walks of life at the ceremony, which will be broadcast live by the China Media Group. In 2014, China's top legislature adopted the decision to establish Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. Since the first Martyrs' Day, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day. This year marks the 77th founding anniversary of the People's Republic of China and the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC. It also marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. A themed exhibition is being held at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing to commemorate that epic military trek. During the Long March, the CPC-led Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution.

item.title: Xi stresses advancing Peaceful China Initiative to safeguard Chinese modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level to ensure steady and sustained progress in Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in his recent instruction on the initiative. In his instruction, Xi stated that since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, significant progress has been made in building a safe China, making the country one of the safest in the world. He emphasized efforts to resolutely pursue a holistic approach to national security and to uphold and strengthen the Party's overall leadership in this area. He also called for efforts to both pursue development and safeguard security, strengthen the legal underpinning, leverage science and technology, and prevent and mitigate all kinds of risks in relevant fields, so as to continuously make the country safer, society more orderly, governance more effective, and the people more satisfied. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a working conference on the initiative held Monday in Beijing. Chen Wenqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Commission for Political and Legal Affairs of the CPC Central Committee, attended the conference and gave a speech. He noted that the Peaceful China Initiative has produced results that have won worldwide recognition and safety has become a distinctive hallmark of China's governance. Chen called for an approach that combines punishment and prevention to create synergy and urged greater efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level. Wang Xiaohong, a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee and minister of public security, pledged that the implementation will focus on key tasks, innovative methods and strengthened foundations at primary levels. China is among the countries with the lowest rates of crime and homicide. A recently released Global Public Security Index Report (2025-2026) showed that the country topped the index with a score of 84.62 points. The findings echo the international perception of China's strong public safety record. More international travelers are experiencing that sense of security firsthand as visa-free access expands, travel services improve and urban support systems are strengthened. At Monday's conference, 60 cities and 160 counties were designated as models for advancing the Peaceful China Initiative and awarded honoring plaques.
